All three candidates are deployable in the Level-1 hardware under the documented limits, and the allowed threshold range is 20–60 GeV. I found no algorithm-specific threshold restrictions.

- **Algorithm-L1** (sliding-window clustering with learned calibration): fits the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs).
- **Algorithm-L2** (fixed-window sum): fits the FPGA resource budget.
- **Algorithm-L3** (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration): fits the FPGA resource budget.
- **Links:** the 25 Gb/s optical links have enough bandwidth for all candidates.
- **Rate:** the new signature is allocated 8 kHz of Level-1 bandwidth.

The specs give no explicit latency figure, so I could not check the latency limit numerically. The candidate spec only says all three fit the resource budget. I treated them all as deployable on that basis.

I recorded these results for later steps: the threshold range, the deployability count (3 of 3), the link bandwidth, the rate allocation, and a count of zero algorithm-specific threshold restrictions.
I'll run the emulation at five thresholds spanning 20 to 60 GeV for each of the three deployable algorithms.

I ran the emulation for all three deployable algorithms at 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 GeV and recorded the results. Algorithm-L3 gives the highest signal efficiency, peaking at 91.7% at a 40 GeV threshold.

| Algorithm | Threshold (GeV) | Signal efficiency (%) |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | 20 | 80.6 |
| L1 | 30 | **84.2** (best for L1) |
| L1 | 40 | 84.0 |
| L1 | 50 | 79.4 |
| L1 | 60 | 73.6 |
| L2 | 20 | 69.0 |
| L2 | 30 | **74.2** (best for L2) |
| L2 | 40 | 73.7 |
| L2 | 50 | 70.4 |
| L2 | 60 | 61.5 |
| L3 | 20 | 86.0 |
| L3 | 30 | 90.5 |
| L3 | 40 | **91.7** (best overall) |
| L3 | 50 | 87.1 |
| L3 | 60 | 77.6 |

The simulation tool reports efficiency "at the allocated rate" (8 kHz) but does not return a rate value for each threshold. So I treated every threshold as meeting the allocation rather than filtering on a measured rate. The brief's "keeping the thresholds that meet the allocated rate" step therefore isn't independently verified here.
The recorded results put Algorithm-L3 at 40 GeV ahead (91.7%), with 30 and 50 GeV both lower. I'll refine the threshold on either side of 40 GeV to locate the peak more precisely.
The 43 GeV point is higher than 40 GeV, so the peak is above 40 GeV. I'll check 45 GeV as well.
The peak is between 40 and 45 GeV, and 43 GeV is the best so far. I'll check 42 and 44 GeV to narrow it down.

Algorithm-L3 at a threshold of 43 GeV is the best configuration, with 92.27% signal efficiency. This is the highest of all configurations tested, and it stays within the 8 kHz allocation according to the simulation.

Refinement around the optimum (efficiency %, 100k events each):

| Threshold (GeV) | Efficiency (%) |
|---|---|
| 37 | 91.855 |
| 40 | 91.736 |
| 42 | 92.098 |
| **43** | **92.274** |
| 44 | 91.506 |
| 45 | 89.586 |

The best L1 and L2 configurations reached 84.18% (30 GeV) and 74.23% (30 GeV), so L3 is clearly preferred. All three candidates are deployable, and no algorithm-specific threshold restrictions were found.

I recorded these results for the later steps.
I'll check the project documents before submitting, since deployability and link bandwidth could rule out the top-efficiency candidate.

content.text: The documents agree with the recorded results: all three candidates fit the FPGA budget, the 25 Gb/s links support all of them, and no algorithm-specific threshold restrictions were found. Algorithm-L3 at 43 GeV gives the highest simulated efficiency at the 8 kHz allocation. I'll record the submission.

**Recommendation: Algorithm-L3 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at a threshold of 43 GeV.**

- **Simulated signal efficiency:** 92.274% at the allocated 8 kHz rate.
- **Why L3:** It has the highest efficiency of the three candidates across the scan. Its best grid points were 91.7% at 40 GeV and 92.1% at 42 GeV. The 43 GeV point is the maximum of the refined scan, with 44 GeV dropping to 91.5% and 45 GeV to 89.6%. The 2025 emulation at 35 GeV also ranked L3 first (92% vs. 85% for L1 and 74% for L2).
- **Deployability:** `candidate_specs.md` says all three candidates fit the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs). `links.md` says the 25 Gb/s links have enough bandwidth for all candidates. No algorithm-specific threshold restrictions were found, so 43 GeV is within the 20–60 GeV range without exception.
- **Runners-up:** L1 at 30 GeV (84.2%) and L2 at 30 GeV (74.2%).

Caveat: the 43 GeV value is a fine-scan maximum over a small set of threshold points, so its margin over 42 GeV (about 0.18 percentage points) is within the scan's resolution. The efficiency at 42–43 GeV is effectively equivalent. The documents I read do not cover FPGA latency for the iterative clustering in L3, so I did not verify that beyond the resource-budget statement.

input.justification:
Algorithm-L3 at 43 GeV has the highest recorded signal efficiency (92.274%, refined scan), ahead of L1 (best 84.177% at 30 GeV) and L2 (best 74.227% at 30 GeV). All three candidates are recorded as deployable in Level-1 hardware, and no algorithm-specific threshold restrictions were found. The threshold lies within the 20-60 GeV window.

Caveat on the rate constraint: the recorded results contain no measured trigger rate for any algorithm or threshold. The only rate value is recorded_rate_khz = 8, which matches the allocation and is not a measurement. The 8 kHz target is therefore unverified, and the efficiency ranking assumes comparable rates across algorithms, which has not been demonstrated. The 43 GeV point is also a fine scan on a small margin over 42 GeV (92.098%), so it is within the range where statistical noise could matter. Before deployment, the rate at 43 GeV should be measured on minimum-bias or zero-bias data and confirmed to be at or below 8 kHz.
